reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend with a defaulted holidays parameter and threads it through every caller, but does not export a shared skipped-day predicate for the daily paths.

duplication.why: The 'weekend or holiday' predicate is written four times (getDateWithSkippedWeekend, getNextDate, getDatesInRange, getUpcomingDates), and getUpcomingDates gains a copy of getNextDate's daily advance-the-recurrence loop.

placement.why: Date-moving logic stays in shared/schedules.ts and the field is added to RecurConfig and parseRecurDate; the daily-skip rule, however, sits in server/schedules/app.ts as well as in shared.

scope.why: Changes are on-topic, though getUpcomingDates also gains new daily-skip behaviour and getDatesInRange widens its window heuristically.

maintainability.why: Any future change to which days are skipped must be repeated in four closures and two daily loops; the adjustmentDays heuristic is ad hoc.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange and shared/schedules.ts getNextDate each define their own isSkippedDay instead of one shared predicate next to getDateWithSkippedWeekend

disguised_duplication.where: The isSkippedDay closure is repeated under the same name in three functions and inlined as a while-condition in getUpcomingDates; the daily-skip loop in getUpcomingDates is a reshaped copy of getNextDate's loop.

one_place.where: Holiday-as-weekend rule lives in getDateWithSkippedWeekend for moves, but the daily-skip rule is re-encoded in getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts), getDatesInRange and getUpcomingDates (server/schedules/app.ts).
